headline: High-risk orchestration pair: LangGraph’s writable, networked default runtime can amplify prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a content-writing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing agent with no isolation or parsing defenses documented; Profile B is a graph orchestrator with stdin/stdout, filesystem, and developer-wired tool nodes. A plausible pathway is B feeding A-generated text back into nodes that treat it as instructions. The shared channel is inferred from B’s orchestration model, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Profile B routes Profile A output into a tool node without provenance checks
IF Profile A content is later parsed as instructions by any downstream node
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A outputs before B consumes them
Insert a 1-step human review before any instruction-like text is executed
Restrict B nodes to treat A output as data, not commands
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile B explicitly reads/writes application-defined files and handles model-provider API keys; Profile A is a content-writing repo with no documented data handling limits. If both share a workspace, B can ingest and forward file contents through broad network egress. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default orchestration, but the exact sensitive data class is not documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Profile A is given access to files that contain sensitive content
IF Profile B is configured to read those files and send them to model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Disable file ingestion for B unless explicitly needed
Redact secrets before any B tool call
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile B has write_filesystem, execute_shell, subprocesses, and broad network egress; Profile A is a content-writing agent with no write surface documented. There is no direct evidence of both modifying the same mutable resource, but B’s shared-state checkpointer and writable files create a realistic conflict surface if A also writes through the same workspace. Uncertainty about A’s runtime pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or checkpointer store
IF Profile A is wrapped in a runtime that also writes artifacts to disk
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Turn off shared checkpointer reuse for concurrent runs
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid running shell steps that mutate shared state
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile B is a stateful orchestrator that can chain nodes and act on developer-defined tools; Profile A is a content-writing agent whose outputs may be treated as authoritative text. That creates a direct cascade path where A’s generated content becomes B’s input and then drives downstream actions without verification. Because B’s defaults include broad tool access, the blast radius can be irreversible, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Profile B uses Profile A output as an input to tool-using nodes
IF no verification or citation-check step is inserted before B acts
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action-taking node
Limit B tools to read-only mode during A-to-B handoff
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Add a stop condition for low-confidence generations
requires-engineering: implement policy gates on downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Profile A, while Profile B handles model-provider API keys and application-defined graph state. The pair does not show a concrete compliance breach pathway from the profiles alone, so only a low residual risk remains. A is not cited for a specific regime because none is declared; B is cited for the only documented compliance-relevant handling.
conditions: IF Profile B stores regulated data in graph state without a matching policy
IF Profile A is used to draft content containing regulated personal data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of graph state
Document retention for B checkpointer data
Restrict A to non-sensitive drafting tasks
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
